govt_bonds.rationale: Changed from 0 to +1. The war-premium unwind in oil (Jan-27 Brent -13% on the week to about $98, US gasoline -33c in a month) pulled down breakevens (10y 2.23%) and real yields (2.60%). The 10y fell about 40bp in a month to about 4.84-4.86%, and the Cleveland Fed nowcasts October core CPI at 0.21% m/m, below September's 0.3%. Treasury kept coupon sizes unchanged for 'the next several quarters', and future increases target 2-10y, so the belly is favoured over the long end. Confidence is low because about 75% of a December hike is priced (it is a hike, not a cut). Nov 10 stacks CPI and the 10y auction, Treasury dropped 'at least' from its guidance, and the BoE, RBA and BoC hiked while the ECB signals December. A US strike on Iran would reverse the oil leg.

gold_precious.rationale: Unchanged at 0. Gold bounced from $3,899 (futures, Oct 30) to about $4,075 on Nov 6. It traded as a real-rate asset: it rose on the post-midterm dollar and yield drop, then fell on strong payrolls and on margin-call selling in the equity rout. About 75% odds of a December hike and Goldman's cut of its end-2026 target to $4,150 (roughly spot) cap the upside. Central-bank buying (321t in Q3, +42% y/y) gives a floor. The miners' outperformance (about 2.8x bullion) is an oversold bounce, and with spot below the Q3 realised price, Q4 margins compress.

regime_notes: Two common factors dominate. First, an AI-buildout and funding shock after the midterm data-centre backlash: SOX -12% on Nov 5, Asian bear markets, and stress concentrated in levered AI credit (Oracle, CoreWeave, neoclouds), while IG and CCC spreads are flat. Second, an Iran war-premium unwind: Jan-27 Brent fell 13% to about $98 because the midterm loss lowered escalation odds. That pulled breakevens and long yields down even as December Fed hike odds stayed near 75% (EFFR 3.88% after September's hike, so it is a hike, not a cut). Central banks are tightening together on energy pass-through (BoE 4%, RBA 4.85%, BoC 2.5%, ECB signalling December), so a sustained oil drop is the main relief valve, and a US strike decision (FGE window mid-November to mid-December) would reverse it. Nov 10 stacks October CPI, the 10y auction, Waller and Bowman, TSMC October sales and SoftBank results. The November payrolls report (Dec 4) comes before the Dec 9 FOMC, so the Dec 11 CR expiry cannot blind the Fed.

red_flags.issue: Treasury removed 'at least' from its coupon-size guidance, and TBAC flags increases in 2H FY27 plus a $2.14tn FY28-29 funding gap. This is term-premium risk for long duration (TLT/long-end) more than for the belly.

AI-linked issuers are paying high-yield-like concessions (Oracle 7-8.65% coupons at Baa2 negative/BBB-; CoreWeave bonds reportedly above 17%). CoreWeave (date unconfirmed, around Nov 10) and Nebius (Nov 12) earnings are near-term spread catalysts for tech-heavy IG/HY ETFs.

Data integrity: December Fed pricing is about 75% for a 25bp HIKE, not a cut (EFFR 3.88% since Sep 17). Brent '$118' is the Oct 30 expiring futures settle and '$135' is the Oct 2 Dated spot print. Continuous BZ=F overstates the weekly drop by about $4.2 because of the contract roll, so use BZF27.
No fund-level event found for KMLM, DBMF, AOM, MUB or MBB (EDGAR scan). Their early-November volume spikes remain unexplained, possibly tax-loss harvesting (unverified).
